_readme: RESEARCH FINDINGS for a Pokemon video game timeline page, read by
scripts/build-video-games.mjs and scripts/sync-game-covers.mjs.
Written from four sources, all read on 2026-08-16.
EVERY FIELD CARRIES ITS SOURCE. Where two sources disagree, both are
kept rather than one being picked. Nothing in this file was typed from
memory.
160 TITLES, AND 'scope' SAYS WHERE THE EDGES ARE. The list started at 79
and was widened on 2026-08-16 to every official release, on the owner's
instruction: mobile, arcade, Pokemon mini, browser, educational and
self-contained LCD games are all in. Five classes are out and every one of
them is named in 'scope.out' rather than described, so nothing is missing
quietly.
THE THREE POKEMON COUNTS ARE DIFFERENT NUMBERS and this file never
collapses them. 'regional_dexes' is the number of ENTRIES in that
game's regional Pokedex, which is not the number of species obtainable
in it and is not the National Pokedex (1,025 species as of Generation
IX). Some games have several regional dexes at once: X and Y has three
(Central 150, Coastal 153, Mountain 151) and Sword and Shield has the
Galar dex plus two DLC dexes. PokeAPI does not publish an 'obtainable
in this game' count, so this file does not state one. Only 26 of the 160
have a PokeAPI version group at all; the rest carry pokedex: null.
A MISSING METASCORE IS NOT A ZERO. 81 of the 160 titles here have no
Metacritic entry and 11 more have a page with no aggregate score, and
those are two different facts that must not be merged. Pokemon Sapphire
has no score while Pokemon Ruby has 82, from the same release, which is
why scores are stored per VERSION and are never copied across a pair.
Read sources.metacritic.note_expansion before quoting 'no Metacritic
entry' for one of the 81 titles added on 2026-08-16: for those it means
a 404 at every address probed, and the addresses are stored.
THOSE TWO NUMBERS WERE 74 AND 19 AND EIGHT TITLES WERE IN THE WRONG ONE.
Corrected 2026-08-16, see sources.metacritic.note_correction. Every one
of the 22 records that said 'no Metascore on page' was re-requested; ten
of them were wrong and the other twelve were confirmed by a 200 with no
aggregateRating block. Nine of the ten were Game Boy and Game Boy Colour
titles that 404 at every address, and the tenth was Pokemon TCG Pocket,
which is not missing a score at all: it has 75.
COVER ART IS NOT ONE SHAPE. 191 files across 160 titles, aspect ratios
0.617 (a Switch keycase) to 2.081 (a wide mobile logo). Any layout that
assumes a single aspect ratio will crop or stretch somebody's artwork.
Intrinsic dimensions are recorded per file for the same reason imgDims()
records them for card scans.
NOT EVERY IMAGE IS A BOX. A phone game has no box and an arcade cabinet
is furniture, so 'kind' is one of 'box art', 'logo', 'cabinet photo' or
'screenshot' and the page labels it rather than calling a cabinet
photograph cover art. Every title in scope has at least one image, so the
hatched no-art box is a fallback for a fetch that failed rather than for a
title that has nothing.
A DELISTED GAME IS STILL A GAME. 'status' is present only where
Bulbapedia's article lead says outright that a title ended or was
delisted, and it carries the sentence it was read from. An ABSENT status
is not a claim that a game is still running: it means the lead did not
say. Several titles here are certainly gone without a sourced date.
MEASURED WEIGHT, so nobody has to guess. The 191 covers re-encoded to
AVIF inside a 320px box are recorded per file; sync-game-covers.mjs
prints the totals it wrote.

bulbapedia.what: Title, platform, generation, category, developer, publisher, release date per region, and the FILENAME of each cover.
bulbapedia.how: MediaWiki API, action=query&prop=revisions, section 0 of each game article, parsed out of {{Infobox game}}.
bulbapedia.note: Values are transcribed from the infobox with wiki markup stripped. Re-release dates that the infobox records in the same field (Virtual Console, Nintendo Classics) are kept, separated by ' | ', rather than dropped. Six fields shipped on 2026-08-16 with an external-link [url label] left in them, against this note's own promise, and were stripped to the label. The page's builder strips the same shapes defensively so a hand edit cannot put raw wikitext back on a live page.

bulbagarden_archives.what: The cover images themselves, and their intrinsic dimensions.
bulbagarden_archives.how: MediaWiki API, prop=imageinfo with iiurlwidth=320 for a server-side thumbnail.
bulbagarden_archives.note: Archives labels these 'Game fair use images'. The artwork is Nintendo's, Game Freak's, Creatures' and The Pokemon Company's; Bulbagarden is the host we read it from, not the owner.

metacritic.what: Metascore and critic review count, per version and per platform.
metacritic.how: Read from the JSON-LD aggregateRating block each /game/<slug>/ page already carries.
metacritic.robots: robots.txt for User-agent: * disallows only /search, /signup, /login, /user, /jl/, /8264/ and /7336/. Game pages are not disallowed. Read 2026-08-16.
metacritic.note_expansion: For the 81 titles added on 2026-08-16, the Metacritic page was requested at the address Metacritic derives from a title (lowercase, non-alphanumerics to hyphens), plus a 'pokemon-' prefixed and a '-version' suffixed variant. A 404 at every variant is recorded as 'no Metacritic entry' and the variants tried are stored in 'probed', so the claim is checkable. That is weaker than a search would be, and Metacritic's robots.txt disallows /search, so a search was not performed.
metacritic.note_correction: TEN RECORDS WERE RE-READ AND CHANGED ON 2026-08-16, and they were changed because data/video-games-PLAN.md disagreed with this file about them. All 22 records that said 'no Metascore on page' were re-requested at https://www.metacritic.com/game/<slug>/ with the status code and the presence of an aggregateRating block recorded. Twelve came back 200 with no aggregateRating and stand unchanged (Sapphire, Stadium, TCG Live, Sleep, Play It, PokeROM, Masters Arena, Team Turbo, Typing Adventure, Camp Pokemon, Playhouse, Smile). Nine came back 404 at every address tried and are now 'no Metacritic entry' with their probes stored: Red, Blue, Yellow, Gold, Silver, Crystal, Pinball, the Game Boy Trading Card Game and Puzzle Challenge. The PLAN was right about those nine and this file was wrong, so the page had been printing 'No Metascore yet' where it should have said 'Not on Metacritic'. THE TENTH IS THE ONE NEITHER FILE HAD RIGHT: Pokemon TCG Pocket has a Metascore of 75 from 9 critic reviews. It was missed because the slug is the abbreviation, pokemon-tcg-pocket, while pokemon-trading-card-game-pocket 404s, and a 404 is exactly what the PLAN recorded as proof of absence. Metacritic's own games sitemap (games.xml, 290 files, fetched in full the same day) is NOT usable as proof of absence either: it omits pokemon-y, pokemon-stadium and pokemon-tcg-pocket, all of which return 200. Only a direct request settles it.

pokeapi.what: Generation, region, count of species introduced per generation, and regional Pokedex entry counts.
pokeapi.note: Already the site's source for data/pokedex.json. Its per-generation new-species counts sum to 1,025, which is exactly the National Pokedex size it reports, so the two are internally consistent.

generation-x.note: PokeAPI publishes nine generations. Generation X exists here only because Bulbapedia labels Pokemon Winds and Waves 'Generation X core series'; no species count, region or Pokedex is published for it yet, so this page states none.

national_dex_total.note: Species with a National Pokedex number. Not forms, not regional variants.

scope.how: Every mainspace article in Bulbapedia's Category:Games that carries an {{Infobox game}} template, minus the five classes below. 259 articles in the category, 201 with an infobox, 160 kept.
scope.in: Core series, side series, spin-offs, mobile and browser releases, arcade cabinets and medal games, Pokemon mini titles, self-contained LCD games, Japanese educational software, and licensee-published Pokemon games. The publisher is printed on every row so a licensed release can be told from a first-party one.

not a Pokemon game: Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS/Wii U
DLC or expansion: Pokémon Sword and Shield Expansion Pass
The Hidden Treasure of Area Zero
demo or prototype: Pokémon Gold and Silver Spaceworld '97 demo
Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Gold Rescue Team
Pokémon Omega Ruby and Pokémon Alpha Sapphire Special Demo Version
Pokémon Sun and Pokémon Moon Special Demo Version
Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Pokémon: Let's Go, Eevee! Demo Version
not a game, by Bulbapedia's own category: Pokémon Project Studio Red and Blue

scope.note: Pokemon Bank, Pokemon HOME and Pokemon TV are not in Category:Games at all and are storage, transfer and video apps rather than games, so they are absent for both reasons. The five 'online games' articles (Pokemon.com, Kids' WB!, Cartoon Network, Daisuki Club, Yahoo! Kids) are list articles covering many unnamed browser minigames rather than one titled release, carry no infobox, and are therefore not rows.
